1. How HTTP request/response works HTTP is a request/response protocol between client and server. Client (browser, curl) opens a TCP connection and sends a request: method (GET, POST), path (/users), headers (Host, Content-Type), optional body. Server receives, routes, processes, and returns a response: status code (200, 404, 500), headers, body. Status classes: 1xx info, 2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client error, 5xx server error. HTTP is stateless — each request stands alone; cookies/tokens add state. HTTPS is HTTP over TLS: encrypted and authenticated. 2.
